_what: Which shape each §8 `S` cell takes, decided by RFC-2026-022 §3's test and recorded here rather than argued in each migration's header.
_why_this_file_exists_before_any_entry: RFC-2026-022 names this file, and four batches are about to classify cells at the same time. If each created it, the merge would be a four-way conflict over a file whose whole purpose is to be one list — so it is created once, empty, with the rules that read it.
Empty is a claim: no §8 `S` cell has been classified yet. The rules below make that claim checkable rather than merely true today.

_shape.cell: the §8 row and column this entry classifies, quoted from the access matrix
_shape.table: table name created by a migration in db/foundation/migrations/, schema-qualified as `app.<name>` or `private.<name>`; an unqualified name means `app`
_shape.why: which half of RFC-2026-022 §3's test the STATEMENT falls on, in a sentence someone can disagree with
_shape.batch: the migration batch that classified it

_not_in_effect: RFC-2026-022 is approved and NOT IN EFFECT: measured 2026-09-08, the only member of app_worker is postgres, which bypasses RLS. A batch classifies its cells here; it does not write a service policy until §7 holds.
_what_batch_110_classified: Batch 110 classifies one cell here: §8.3's "Raw token/webhook SELECT", which RFC-2026-022 §3's own table assigns to batches 110 and 131 and calls DISCOVERED. 131 owns the same cell for the payment inbox and adds its own row; the register keys on (cell, statement), so two rows for one cell on two tables is the shape §5/1 describes rather than a duplicate.
_a_private_table_needed_the_rule_to_say_: The `table` field was documented as "unqualified table name in the app schema", and this cell's table is in `private` — §3.1 puts "raw webhook" there by name and §14's gate checklist requires it not be exposed. The rule could not express the entry it was written to receive. It now accepts a schema-qualified name and resolves an unqualified one to `app`, which changes no verdict for a cell in `app` and is asserted in test-kits/db/foundation-contract.test.mjs in both directions.

cells.why: The statement a processor issues is "the next unprocessed delivery", and it contains no workspace term because WHICH workspace is what reading the row resolves. Under RFC-2026-022 §3's operational test, adding the confinement term to its WHERE does not narrow the same work — it turns "the unprocessed webhook" into "the unprocessed webhook of a tenant I already knew", which is not the work. The schema says the same thing: private.meta_webhook_inbox.workspace_id is NULLABLE, because a delivery arrives before anything knows whose it is and resolution can fail, and batch 110's apply-time block refuses a later NOT NULL.

cells.cell: §8.4 Usage ledger INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (`S/N`) — the `S` half, which is the INSERT
cells.why: The statement's workspace is an INPUT and not an output. RFC-2026-022 §3 already classes this cell CARRIED, giving the reason 'a reservation is made against a known quota'; applying §3's own operational form to the STATEMENT gives a stronger one. Add `and workspace_id = (select nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid)` to this INSERT's WITH CHECK and it still writes the same row, because CTR-USG-001 makes attribution.workspace_id a REQUIRED property of the envelope and composes the dedupe_key with that same workspace as its second segment -- 061_metering.sql then constrains the key to start with the row's own workspace, so the workspace is something the row says twice before any policy reads it. Nothing here is a claim about the confinement term being a boundary: RFC-2026-022 §5/4 measured that app_worker can set the setting the policy would read, so the term is containment against defects in the service's own code and never tenant isolation of the service path. NO POLICY IS WRITTEN: the decision is approved and NOT IN EFFECT (§5/8, and the `_not_in_effect` note above), so this row classifies the cell and authorises nothing. §8.4's UPDATE and DELETE half is `N` for the service too, which is why this table has one entry and not three; app.usage_reservations and app.quota_buckets have none at all, because §8 has no row for either in any of its four matrices and inventing a `cell` value would be a claim about the access matrix made in a lint file.

cells.cell: §8.4 Notification insert/delivery state | N | N | N | N | N | S
cells.why: The workspace is an INPUT. §8.4's other notification row marks "Own notification SELECT/mark read" `O`, so an inbox row cannot be addressed at all without knowing whose it is -- and app.notifications carries user_id NOT NULL beside workspace_id NOT NULL, both in the INSERT's own VALUES list. Applying RFC-2026-022 §3's operational form: add `and workspace_id = (select nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid)` to the WITH CHECK and the statement still addresses the same work -- "insert a notification for this recipient in this workspace" is unchanged, because the server resolved both before forming it. Nothing here discovers a workspace by reading, which is the half of §3's test that would make it DISCOVERED. RFC-2026-022 §3's own table classifies this cell for batch 051 as CARRIED with the reason "recipient and workspace are inputs"; this row is that classification checked against the statement rather than accepted from the table.

cells.cell: §8.4 Notification insert/delivery state | N | N | N | N | N | S
cells.why: The delivery-state half of the same cell, classified separately because RFC-2026-022 §7.2 keys the register on (cell, STATEMENT) and never on the table alone -- the asset-hard-purge row in §3's table is BOTH shapes for exactly that reason. The statement is `update app.notifications set delivery_state = ..., delivery_failure_class = ... where id = $1`: it names one row by its id, and that row's workspace came back with it from the send that produced the report. Adding the confinement term to its WHERE changes nothing about which row it addresses. Contrast batch 050's claim on app.jobs, which is DISCOVERED because `for update skip locked` on the next due row has no workspace term to add without changing what the work is; a delivery report is written about a notification the service already holds, not selected across tenants by age or readiness.
